title: From Steane to A7: Quantum Codes from Invariant States
abstract: We construct a two-parameter family of single-error-correcting seven-ququart codes with transversal $\tilde{A_7}$ symmetry, realizing the finite component of a two-qubit super-golden gate set. These $((7,4,3))_4$ codes encode two logical qubits and support non-Clifford operations by applying the same gate to each physical ququart.   Our method constructs invariant parent states rather than searching directly for a codespace. For $n$ systems of local dimension $q$, suppose the local symmetry is a unitary $t$-group and the permutation symmetry is $t$-transitive. Maximal mixing of all marginals on at most $t$ sites is then equivalent to linear equations in Schur--Weyl sector weights. Every feasible solution yields parents of pure distance at least $t+1$; puncturing one site produces a $q$-dimensional code of distance at least $t$ with the prescribed local symmetry acting transversally.   Steane and the nonstabilizer Fake Steane code reveal why the construction leaves continuous freedom. They share the same prescribed transversal Clifford and permutation symmetries, and their eight-qubit purifications lie on a circle: error correction fixes two invariant-sector norms but leaves the relative phase free. Keeping the same permutation group and replacing Clifford symmetry by $\tilde{A_7}$ $\leq SU(4)$ gives three fixed sector norms and two free relative phases, producing the new ququart family.
summary: This paper develops a powerful method to construct quantum error-correcting codes by analyzing invariant states derived from symmetry constraints. It successfully constructs a new two-parameter family of seven-ququart codes with $	ilde{A}_7$ symmetry, extending beyond previously known codes like the Steane code.
main_problem: The paper aims to construct quantum error-correcting codes with specific transversal symmetries, particularly $	ilde{A}_7$, realizing the finite component of a two-qubit super-golden gate set.
main_result: A two-parameter family of single-error-correcting seven-ququart codes, $((7, 4, 3))_4$, is constructed, showing that the Steane and Fake Steane codes are specific points within this continuous family.
method: The construction method involves building invariant parent states by solving linear equations derived from Schur-Weyl sector weights, rather than searching directly for the codespace.
model_or_system: The system is a quantum error-correcting code defined on ququart systems, analyzed using invariant states in the tensor product space $V \otimes n$ under the combined action of local unitary-design symmetry ($G \le SU(q)$) and permutation symmetry ($\Sigma \le S_n$).
key_observables: Code parameters $((7, 4, 3))_4$, the continuous parameter $	heta$, and the sector weights $(p_8, p_{44})$ determined by moment equations.
important_parameters: The local dimension $q=4$, the number of sites $n=7$ (for the code), and the symmetry group $	ilde{A}_7 \le SU(4)$.
main_assumptions: The method relies on the equivalence between maximal mixing of marginals on $\le t$ sites and the feasibility of a linear system in Schur-Weyl sector weights.
figures_summary: The notes mention TABLE I comparing the Steane and $	ilde{A}_7$ families, and Equation (15) providing the unique solution for the sector weights in the $	ilde{A}_7$ case.
paper_structure: The paper develops the general theory by relating code construction to linear feasibility problems in Schur-Weyl weights. It then applies this theory to the specific case of $	ilde{A}_7$ symmetry, showing how the resulting parent state yields the desired two-parameter family of codes.
why_interesting: The rigorous mathematical framework connecting symmetry constraints (like $	ilde{A}_7$) to the existence and parameters of quantum codes is highly relevant for designing fault-tolerant quantum computation protocols.
